clue.text: Chinese group departs after warning shot

indicators.note: the Chinese group and departs come after the warning, so they follow it

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
the Han are China's majority ethnic group
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone fires a warning shot and a Chinese group leaves in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' at the end looks like part of 'warning shot', but it is the definition, a tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a forehand is a stroke played with the palm facing forward, one kind of shot.

clue.text: Fellow abseiling loses footing on ice

indicators.note: the footing of a word is its last letter, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rappel is the American term for abseil, descending a rope

explanation.surface: A climber abseiling down a frozen face slips and loses his footing on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses footing' takes the last letter L off RAPPEL. 'on ice' is not where the fellow is; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A frappé is a drink served chilled or poured over crushed ice; the French word means iced.

clue.text: Dish out pleasure, not a kick in the teeth

indicators.note: to dish out is to deal out or distribute, so the letters are rearranged
not a means the letter a is taken from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone hands out pleasure, which is the opposite of a kick in the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the A from PLEASURE; 'Dish out' rearranges the remaining PLESURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A repulse is a rebuff or rejection, the same humiliating setback as a kick in the teeth.

clue.text: Half the world is into cannabis, I say

indicators.note: into puts the word is inside the cannabis plant

parts.note: hemp is the cannabis plant
'Here!' and 'I say!' are both calls for attention

explanation.surface: An exclamation that half the world's population uses cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is into' looks like 'enjoys'; in fact 'is' is the piece and 'into' the insertion signal. 'I say' gives HERE, as both are ways of calling for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemisphere is one half of the globe, northern or southern, eastern or western.

clue.text: There's no chance of solvers entering unacceptable term

indicators.note: entering puts the solvers' possessive between the other two pieces

parts.note: 'not on' is informal British for unacceptable
life is a prison term, a life sentence
your means belonging to you, the solvers addressed by the clue

explanation.surface: A setter flatly refuses to let solvers into some forbidden term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' is everyday British slang for not acceptable, and a life term is a life sentence in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, saying something will certainly never happen.

clue.text: Excellent suggestion might finally work

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of might

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An outstanding piece of advice that may, in the end, actually succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal synonym for first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Billy's head down in the swimming pool

indicators.note: the head of the word is sent down to the bottom, its first letter moving to the end

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool

explanation.surface: Someone dives head first into the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head down' moves the L of LIDO from the start to the end. 'Billy's' is Billy is, the 's a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Idol is the British punk and rock singer, so the surname completes the name Billy.

clue.text: Split receipts on holiday

parts.note: the take is the money received, the takings
someone off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: A business divides its takings while the owners are away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like dividing the receipts; it is slang for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is slang for leave in a hurry, and take off means to depart suddenly.

clue.text: After being overthrown, Napoleon's exile too easy to bear?

indicators.note: overthrown turns everything upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Napoleon was exiled to the island of Elba in 1814
trop is French for too, the French flavour set by Napoleon

explanation.surface: Napoleon, deposed, may have found exile on his island too easy to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too' must be read in French, the language Napoleon's name implies; the whole run is overthrown as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portable is light enough to be carried, so easy to bear in the literal sense of carry.

clue.text: It helps you hear note played relatively quietly

parts.note: A is a musical note
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical marking for moderately quiet

explanation.surface: A musical note, played fairly softly, is still audible with help.
explanation.definitionFit: An amp, short for amplifier, boosts sound so that it can be heard.

clue.text: Harry wrote "Markle, I'm no different from Smith"

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Prince Harry writes to Meghan Markle protesting he is no different from any ordinary Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince; it is the anagram signal, rearranging WROTE MARKLE. 'I'm no different from' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith is a craftsman who forges and shapes metal, such as a blacksmith.

clue.text: Smear top of nasty verruca in gel — it'll show improvement

indicators.note: smearing spreads and messes things up, so the letters are rearranged
the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Treatment instructions: dab the head of a nasty verruca with gel and it will get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smear' looks like an instruction; it rearranges N, VERRUCA and IN GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A learning curve is a graph of progress against practice, showing how skill improves over time.

clue.text: Feast always started with bananas and plums

indicators.note: the anagram comes first, the always piece following it
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: ay, also spelt aye, is an old and Scots word meaning always or ever

explanation.surface: A feast that always begins with bananas and plums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit beside the plums but rearranges AND PLUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Sunday is a Christian feast day, the Sunday before Easter, marking Christ's entry into Jerusalem.

clue.text: Low point for every drink

parts.note: a col is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks
a means per, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: Someone at their lowest reaches for a drink every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a sweet carbonated soft drink flavoured with kola nut.

clue.text: Prevent wandering of his cool hand

parts.note: to pen animals is to shut them in so they cannot stray
man's means belonging to a man, i.e. his
hip is slang for cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: Advice to stop his relaxed hand from straying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' looks like a body part; it means handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a person's handwriting, and penmanship is the art or style of writing by hand.

clue.text: Maybe Pavarotti right away gets to grips with church music

indicators.note: gripping something holds it inside, so the church is held
right away tells you R, for right, goes away

parts.note: Luciano Pavarotti was a famous tenor, so he is an example

explanation.surface: Pavarotti promptly tackles some church music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once'; it removes R from TENOR, leaving TENO, which then holds CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a style of electronic dance music with a fast repetitive beat.

clue.text: New feud brewing among the Spanish poor

indicators.note: among places the stirred letters inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: a feud that is brewing is stirring and forming, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A new feud is brewing among the Spanish poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges FEUD to EDFU, which goes 'among' EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful can mean needy, lacking the necessities of life, as the poor are.

clue.text: Narcissus slid off a diving-board, absorbed by reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters read backwards
something absorbed by the words sits within their letters

explanation.surface: Narcissus slides off a diving-board, so absorbed was he in his reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Narcissus fell for his reflection, so the surface works; the reflection is the reversal of LIDOFFAD, held 'absorbed by' the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the botanical name of the daffodil genus.

clue.text: On edge, lawyer rejected potential suitor

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run of letters is reversed

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a rim is an edge
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A nervous lawyer turns down a would-be suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses RE RIM DA.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone romantically attracted to a person, who may go on to court them.

clue.text: Accepting ring, end up married — as did the pussycat?

indicators.note: accepting takes the ring into the middle
in a down answer up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
wed means married
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: Echoes The Owl and the Pussycat, who married with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AIM to MIA; MIA plus WED 'Accepting' O. In Edward Lear's poem the Owl and the Pussy-cat marry with a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call is a miaow, so the pussycat miaowed.

clue.text: A Scottish idiot set my punt adrift

indicators.note: a punt set adrift floats loose, so its letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Some fool from Scotland pushed my punt off into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set ... adrift' rearranges MY PUNT; 'set' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Numpty is Scottish slang for a fool or a stupid person.

clue.text: Show nipple pierced by husband; sore, but not very

indicators.note: a pierced nipple has something through it, so the husband goes inside

parts.note: a teat is a nipple

indicators.note: but not very means the word for very is taken out of sore

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired

explanation.surface: A husband's nipple piercing: sore, but not very.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not very' removes SO from SORE, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is drama staged as a show, and a show is a theatrical performance.

clue.text: Royal house opening for everyone to see inside

indicators.note: inside puts the film rating within the opening

parts.note: a start is an opening
U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A royal residence opens its doors so the public can look inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for everyone to see' is the U certificate, Britain's rating for films fit for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were the dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England, a royal family.

clue.text: Boring, with no relief

definitions.meaning: dull and lifeless, as in a dull performance
level, without raised features or hills

explanation.surface: A tedious event offers no respite.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull and uninteresting, and also level ground without any relief features.

clue.text: Bother, the candlestick's covered in grime

indicators.note: covered in grime means the grime surrounds the candlestick

parts.note: dirt is grime
a sconce is a wall bracket holding candles

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that the candlestick is filthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert is to unsettle or fluster someone, the same sense as bother.

clue.text: Sore losers forget they were ever in last place

indicators.note: ever in last place takes the letter standing last in each word

explanation.surface: Bad losers forget they ever finished last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore losers' reads as one phrase, but 'Sore' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore spot.

clue.text: Unlikely to be silly, because of dodgy heart

parts.note: down to means due to, as in it was down to him

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or unreliable, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A person is too cautious to fool around because of a weak heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical, sensible person is grounded and realistic, not given to foolishness.

clue.text: It's made by boiling water, endlessly

definitions.text: It's made by boiling water, endlessly

indicators.note: boiling water churns, so the letters are stirred
endlessly drops both ends, keeping only the middle letters

explanation.surface: A drink made by pouring boiling water, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips W and R from WATER, leaving ATE; 'boiling' rearranges it. The whole clue also describes the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is brewed by pouring boiling water over leaves, and the British make it all day long.

clue.text: Occasionally, lines entering gents; more often, here

indicators.note: entering puts the picked letters inside the men

parts.note: lads are young men, gents

indicators.note: occasionally takes letters now and then, every other one

explanation.surface: A sign about lines going into the gents, and longer queues somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' looks like the men's toilet; it means LADS. The definition jokes that queues form at the women's toilet more often.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladies is the women's public toilet, where queues form more often than at the gents.

clue.text: Headgear protects several bits of PE assistant

indicators.note: protects means wraps around, so the helmet surrounds the letters
several bits of means the letters of PE are taken one at a time and placed separately

parts.note: a helmet is protective headgear
PE is physical education; its letters go in one by one
the second letter of PE, physical education, goes in on its own

explanation.surface: A helmet shields parts of a PE assistant in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'several bits of' signals that P and E go in separately: HEL-P-ME-E-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmeet is a helpful companion or partner, a helper.
